winner.text: Your $2k paycheck disappears faster than you think. Here's exactly where.
winner.reasoning: This hook combines genuine curiosity gap (the mystery of where money goes) with immediate relevance—$2k is the exact salary range 22-year-olds in entry-level jobs recognize. script.script:
[HOOK - 0-3 sec]

[ON-SCREEN TEXT: "WHERE YOUR $2K PAYCHECK GOES"]

Your $2k paycheck hits the account on Friday. By Wednesday, it's gone. And you have no idea where.

[PAUSE]

[PROBLEM - 3-8 sec]

[ON-SCREEN TEXT: "THE DAMAGE:"]

Rent: $800. Groceries: $200. That's $1k already. Then your brain short-circuits. Uber Eats instead of cooking? $120. One "quick" shopping trip? $180. Coffee every morning? $80. That random subscription you forgot about? $15. Drinks with friends? $200.

[CUT]

[VALUE - 8-15 sec]

Here's the blunt truth: you're not making a money problem—you're making a *visibility* problem.

[ON-SCREEN TEXT: "3 MOVES:"]

One: Track every single transaction for ONE week. Yeah, it sucks. But you'll see the leaks.

Two: Set up auto-transfers the DAY you get paid. Move $400 to savings before your brain says "but what if I need it for brunch?"

Three: Delete your food delivery apps. Just one. You'll survive. And you'll keep like $80.

[PAUSE]

[CTA - 15-17 sec]

That's an extra $500 a month. Do the math. Save this before payday hits and you forget again.
script.viewer_takeaway: A clear breakdown of where money leaks on a $2k paycheck, plus three immediately actionable fixes—track spending, automate savings, cut one subscription—to keep an extra $500/month.

justifications.clarity: Hook lands immediately with relatable problem ($2k gone by Wednesday), dollar amounts and specific leaks make the point concrete, not abstract.
justifications.retention: Rapid cuts between problem/visuals and the satisfaction of seeing the 3-move solution creates forward momentum, but lacks emotional peak moments.
justifications.save_potential: Specific, actionable moves + concrete math ($500/month result) make this highly bookmark-worthy for payday prep.
justifications.shareability: Relatable pain point will resonate in group chats, but lacks the memetic angle or shock value that drives organic sharing.
justifications.audience_fit: Directly mirrors Gen Z first-job cash flow anxiety (rent + impulsive spending), language and tone match the demographic precisely.
justifications.cta_strength: Clear (save this) and timed well (before payday), but framed as accountability reminder rather than urgency driver.

weaknesses.issue: The $500/month payoff feels disconnected from the moves—no bridge showing how $80 coffee + $120 delivery actually equals $500 without adding new categories.
weaknesses.fix: Rewrite 14-15 sec as: 'Delete delivery apps? $80. Stop impulse shopping? $180. Skip daily coffee? $60. Auto-save the rest. That's $500 you actually keep. Compounded over a year? $6k for literally changing three habits.'

weaknesses.issue: Move Two (auto-transfer) lacks specificity—$400 is arbitrary with no logic tied to the rent/essentials breakdown shown earlier.
weaknesses.fix: Rewrite 12-13 sec as: 'TWO: Auto-transfer $600 day one. (That's rent plus buffer.) Move it before you see it. Your brain can't spend what it can't see.'

weaknesses.issue: The 'delete one app' ask in Move Three feels weak—real friction comes from having the app available, so deletion alone won't stop redownloading.
weaknesses.fix: Rewrite 13-14 sec as: 'THREE: Delete the app AND block the website on your phone. One swipe to order is why you're broke. Make yourself wait 48 hours if you really want it—spoiler: you won't.'

captions: your $2k paycheck hits friday. by wednesday? gone. here's the 3-move system to keep an extra $500 every month. save this before payday hits 🚨
$2k disappears in 5 days and you don't even know why. track, automate, delete. that's it. save this for friday. your future self will thank you 💰
growth.final_call_reason: Strong clarity and audience fit, but the three moves lack internal logic consistency—auto-transfer amount needs justification tied to expenses, and the $500 payoff calculation bridge is missing, making the promise feel hollow despite strong execution elsewhere.
